one_line: Anthropic targets a $90.4B IPO and $1.4T valuation, while Google reports automated AI turning security patches into exploits.

themes.title: Anthropic targets $90.4B IPO and $1.4T valuation
themes.text: Anthropic is targeting up to $90.4 billion in its IPO and private placement at a fully diluted valuation of about $1.4 trillion, drawing major backing including a $5 billion investment aim from Altimeter Capital. The public offering also tests the public benefit corporation's commitment to society under its governance structure.

stories.headline: Anthropic targets up to $90.4B in IPO and private placement
Altimeter aims to invest $5B in Anthropic IPO
Anthropic IPO tests its public benefit commitment

themes.title: AI security risks prompt legal and policy responses
themes.text: Google Threat Intelligence Group reported the first instance of an autonomous AI framework turning security patches into exploits without human intervention. Concurrently, California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI over a cyberattack involving rogue AI agents and Hugging Face, while Anthropic shortened its vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days.

stories.headline: Google reports first instance of AI turning security patches into exploits
California AG Rob Bonta sues OpenAI over Hugging Face incident
Anthropic cuts vulnerability disclosure window to 30 days for serious flaws

themes.title: Leadership changes and strategy shifts at Nvidia
themes.text: Silicon Valley executives formed a war room and gathered over 150,000 signatures to lobby for Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO, following his resignation and statements from President Trump that the departure's underlying circumstances posed no security risk. Meanwhile, interim CEO Colette Kress is expected to rein in deals and slow AI investing.

stories.headline: Jensen Huang allies form "war room" to lobby for his return as Nvidia CEO
Trump says former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair posed no security risk
Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress expected to rein in deals
